observation_summary: The Regula Falsi solver fails with a TooManyEvaluationsException because it enters an infinite loop when the update formula fails to produce a new, distinct approximation due to floating-point precision limits. The algorithm lacks a check for this stagnation.
hypothesis: The Regula Falsi solver implementation in BaseSecantSolver lacks a mechanism to detect when the algorithm stagnates due to floating-point precision limitations. Specifically, when the update formula produces a new approximation 'x' that is identical to the current bound 'x1', the solver continues to evaluate the same point repeatedly until the maximum evaluation count is reached. This is a deficiency in the algorithm's control flow logic, which fails to handle the edge case of non-progressing intervals.
prediction: The implementation will continue to loop indefinitely (or until max evaluations) when the calculated 'x' equals 'x1', as there is no conditional check to detect this stagnation and force an interval update.
